sources.entry: SaneHosts - System-level ad and tracker blocker via /etc/hosts with 200+ curated blocklists and Touch ID protection.

summary.one_liner: SaneHosts is a native macOS app for managing the /etc/hosts file, letting you pick a protection level (ad, tracker, and optional category blocking) and activate it without using Terminal.
summary.what_it_does: The app organizes hosts configurations as profiles with color tags, and offers five protection levels (Essentials, Family Safe, Focus Mode, Privacy Shield, Kitchen Sink) that each bundle curated blocklists. Users can import from 200+ curated sources or custom HTTPS blocklist URLs, merge profiles with deduplication, and export profiles as standard .hosts files. Activating a profile requires macOS admin authorization, flushes the DNS cache, and keeps automatic backups (3 per profile). A menu bar item allows quick profile switching, and a "Turn Off Protection" action reverts changes. The README says it handles lists of 100K+ entries with search and filter, and shows URL health indicators for blocklist sources.
use_cases: block ads and trackers system-wide on a Mac
set up parental content blocking for a family computer
block distracting social media sites during focus time
import and merge community blocklists into hosts files
how_to_run: Download the signed, notarized app from sanehosts.com
Start the free 14-day trial inside the app
Choose a protection level and activate it (admin password required)
stack: SaneUI (resolved from GitHub when building from source)
notable: Five preset protection levels that bundle curated blocklists by strictness
Requires system authorization for every hosts change rather than silent edits
Automatic backups (3 per profile) with recovery of corrupted profiles
Listed as an officially listed tool in the upstream StevenBlack/hosts repository
Local-first privacy with limited anonymous product events
caveats: Free 14-day trial, then a one-time purchase is needed to keep using all features
Source code is under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0, which is free for personal use and experimentation only
